attempts.label: SPARC:60
attempts.entry_title: Vagus nerve morphology of human, pig and rat (Pelot et al. 2020)
attempts.summary: Most of the paper's cross-species comparisons of vagus nerve morphology hold up in this rat dataset with the authors' human and pig data: rat nerves are about ten times smaller, human and pig nerves have similar diameters, pigs have many more fascicles, and perineurium thickens with fascicle size, most in humans. Cervical fascicles are larger than subdiaphragmatic ones in all three species, but not significantly in pigs (p = 0.055) under the test matching the paper. The perineurium relationship differs between levels in human and pig, where the paper, naming no test, reports none. Of minor claims, the literature comparisons hold in part, the absence of age trends fails on uncorrected tests, and the carotid sheath bundles are untested.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Pelot, Goldhagen, Cariello, Musselman, Clissold, Ezzell and Grill (2020) on SPARC dataset 60, version 5, which holds the segmented traces of nine left cervical and nine anterior subdiaphragmatic rat vagus nerve samples and the paper's MATLAB code. The rat nerve and fascicle diameters, fascicle counts, tissue proportions and perineurium fit are measured from the traces with the paper's method. The comparisons with human and pig use the paper's sister datasets, SPARC 65 (human traces), 64 (pig Masson's trichrome) and 89 (pig anti-fibronectin), for the mixed model ANOVAs, Tukey tests and perineurium fits, and Supplement 4 of the paper for the literature comparisons.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Pelot et al. (2020) from SPARC dataset 60 and its sister datasets

outcomes.statement: The dataset holds the rat samples the paper analysed, segmented traces of nine left cervical and nine anterior subdiaphragmatic vagus nerve samples from Sprague-Dawley rats, 4F and 5M at each level, from 10 rats (5M/5F).
outcomes.source: Materials and Methods, Sample Collections, paragraph 1, and Imaging and Image Analysis, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: We analyzed all left cervical (4F/5M) and anterior subdiaphragmatic (4F/5M) rat VN samples.
outcomes.notes: Nine cervical and nine subdiaphragmatic samples, 4F and 5M at each level, from 10 Sprague-Dawley rats (5M, 5F), aged 75 to 268 days, body mass 381.1 +/- 118.4 g (SD, n = 10), as the Methods give. Cervical samples are all left. The subdiaphragmatic samples are described in samples.xlsx without the side, which only the readme gives as anterior. R18 has only a cervical sample (R18-1) and R26 only a subdiaphragmatic one, as the Methods describe. No right cervical or posterior samples are deposited (the code's lists for them are empty). The 18 PeriMask arrays are all distinct. The readme gives ages 65 to 268 days, subjects.xlsx 75 to 268.

outcomes.statement: Effective nerve diameter differs across species and across nerve levels, with no detected interaction of species and level.
outcomes.quote: The nerve diameter differed across species ( p < 0.0001; F = 577.1) and nerve levels ( p = 0.0030; F = 11.01), but we did not detect an interaction of species and level ( p = 0.1085; F = 2.445).

statistics.n: 9 cervical and 9 subdiaphragmatic samples per species (human, pig MT, rat)

outcomes.notes: Unbounded REML (subject variance -0.052, residual 0.127) with Kenward-Roger tests on the observed information gives species F = 577.0 (p < 0.0001), level F = 11.01 (p = 0.0030) and interaction F = 2.4455 (p = 0.1085), against the paper's 577.1, 11.01 (p = 0.0030) and 2.445 (p = 0.1085). On the expected information F = 587.3, 11.03 and 2.450 (interaction p = 0.103). The Wald F values are 599.6, 11.05 and 2.455; with Satterthwaite, residual or subject-based degrees of freedom the interaction p is 0.108, 0.097 or 0.104. With the subject variance bounded at zero (statsmodels REML) the interaction is significant (F = 3.71, p = 0.024), which would make the claim partially reproduced; an ordinary ANOVA gives p = 0.035. The human data are measured here from the traces of SPARC:65 (version 6) with the paper's method, and match its code's output file exactly; the pig MT values come from the per-fascicle output file of SPARC:64 (version 4, files/code/PigVNMorphology_OutputMetrics.mat), not from its traces.
deviations: The Methods fit the mixed models in JMP Pro 14.3.0 and do not give its settings. The fit here is REML with unbounded variance components, JMP's default, which statsmodels does not offer, and effects and Tukey contrasts are tested with Kenward-Roger F tests and degrees of freedom computed on the observed REML information (the Hessian of the REML log-likelihood), written in vagus.py and checked on a balanced split-plot design. This is an assumption about the paper's settings, adopted after round 2 because it gives the paper's F and p for all nine effects the paper reports (F within 0.4%, p to the digits printed, degrees of freedom within 1 of those the paper's F and p imply; nerve diameter 577.0, 11.01 and 2.4455 against 577.1, 11.01 and 2.445). Kenward-Roger on the expected information (the main test in round 2), Satterthwaite, residual and subject-based degrees of freedom and a bounded fit are variants.
Human from SPARC:65 and pig from SPARC:64, the paper's Pelot et al. (2020a and f) by their titles; the claims file gives no identifiers.

outcomes.statement: All three species have larger fascicles at the cervical than at the subdiaphragmatic level.
outcomes.quote: All species had larger fascicles at the cervical level ( p < 0.0001 for humans; p = 0.0009 for pigs; p = 0.0234 for rats).
outcomes.notes: Cervical larger in each species. With Kenward-Roger on the observed information, the test that gives the paper's F and p, Tukey p human 0.00002, pig 0.055, rat 0.045 (paper < 0.0001, 0.0009, 0.0234), two of three species; with the code's rat values human 0.00003, pig 0.060, rat 0.0093, again two. The outcome verified in rounds 1 and 2, reproduced, rested on Kenward-Roger on the expected information, human 0.000001, pig 0.012, rat 0.044 (code's rat values pig 0.013, rat 0.0089); round 3 agreed with the change to partially reproduced. Of the ten combinations of test and rat values printed, six give three species and four give two (the observed-information test with either rat rule, Satterthwaite with the code's rat values, pig p = 0.053, and subjects minus parameters with the largest fascicle, rat p = 0.068). The pig contrast has 3.74 degrees of freedom on the observed information and 7.55 on the expected, mostly from the sample variance term (138257 against 243007). No variant gives the paper's pig p of 0.0009, which with this contrast's t of 4.77 would need 24.6 degrees of freedom. Residual degrees of freedom give pig 0.00001 and rat 0.043, the bounded fit pig 0.00001 and rat 0.043. A rat-only mixed model (unbounded REML, Kenward-Roger) gives p = 1.7e-07 for the largest fascicle and 0.00033 for the code's values; a paired t test on the 8 rats with both levels gives p = 8.0e-07.

The outcome rests on the choice of test. In round 2 Kenward-Roger on the expected information was the assumption; the verifier showed the paper's degrees of freedom do not support it, and the test on the observed information, which reproduces the paper's F and p, is adopted in its place. Under it the outcome is partially reproduced, proposed after round 2 and agreed in round 3. This test does not give the paper's within-species level contrasts (pig p 0.055 against 0.0009, rat 0.045 against 0.0234), the one set of the paper's Tukey p values it misses.

outcomes.statement: The monofascicular rat nerves have diameters close to that of a single human or pig fascicle.
outcomes.quote: The monofascicular rat nerves were ∼10× smaller, and their diameters approximated the diameter of a single human or pig fascicle.
outcomes.notes: Reading (a) the rat mean nerve diameter lies between the pig and human mean fascicle diameters at both levels (257.7 between 154.5 and 354.8 um; 135.2 between 110.1 and 163.5 um); reading (b) within the range of their fascicles at both levels.

outcomes.statement: Endoneurium is a larger share of the human nerve cervically (32 +/- 7.9%) than subdiaphragmatically (8.8 +/- 5.3%), while in pigs it is more even across levels (27 +/- 5.3% and 20 +/- 4.0%, MT); perineurium follows the same trends (human 8.9 +/- 2.5% and 3.4 +/- 1.6%, pig 5.1 +/- 1.8% and 4.0 +/- 0.5%).
outcomes.quote: The human endoneurium occupied a larger proportion of the nerve at the cervical level (32 ± 7.9%) than at the subdiaphragmatic level (8.8 ± 5.3%) whereas the endoneurial proportions were more consistent across levels in pigs, slightly lower than in the human cervical VN (27 ± 5.3% at the cervical level and 20 ± 4.0% at the subdiaphragmatic level for the MT micrographs ... These same trends between species and levels were present for the proportion of perineurium (8.9 ± 2.5% and 3.4 ± 1.6% at the cervical and subdiaphragmatic levels in humans; 5.1 ± 1.8% and 4.0 ± 0.5% in pigs).
outcomes.notes: Endoneurium human 32.23 +/- 7.9 and 8.83 +/- 5.3%, pig MT 26.63 +/- 5.27 and 20.29 +/- 3.98%; perineurium human 8.87 +/- 2.47 and 3.42 +/- 1.59%, pig IF 5.07 +/- 1.75 and 4.00 +/- 0.52%; all eight within the stated SDs. Pig IF endoneurium 24.9 and 18.1%, about 2 points below MT as the paper says.
deviations: Pig MT endoneurium from the per-fascicle diameters of SPARC:64's output file (sum of circle areas over the nerve's circle area, equal to the traces' areas); pig IF perineurium from the per-sample proportions of SPARC:89's PigIFMorphology.mat, not recomputed from its traces.
outcomes.where: SPARC Portal, Pelot et al. (2020a) for human, (2020f) for pig MT and (2020b) for pig IF; identifiers not in the text read

outcomes.statement: In rats the ratio of mean subdiaphragmatic to mean cervical endoneurial area is 0.32 and the ratio of mean nerve diameters is 0.68.
outcomes.quote: The ratios of the mean endoneurial area of the subdiaphragmatic VN to the cervical VN were 0.20, 0.42, and 0.32 for human, pig, and rat, respectively ... where the ratios of the mean diameter of the subdiaphragmatic VN to the cervical VN were 0.87, 0.75, and 0.68 for human, pig, and rat, respectively.
outcomes.notes: Reading (b), all segmented fascicles and the connective tissue boundary for the three multifascicular samples, gives 0.317 and 0.678, within 10% of 0.32 and 0.68. Reading (a), the largest fascicle as in the statistics, gives 0.270 and 0.525, both outside; the Results' means give 0.519. So the Discussion's rat ratios use a different tissue boundary than the Results' rat statistics. Supplement 4's rat subdiaphragmatic endoneurial area (0.0155 mm2) is also the all-fascicle area, though its note says rat data are for the largest fascicle.
deviations: The claim holds under one of the two readings the criterion lists; measured gives reading (b), the only one that matches.

outcomes.statement: The ratio of mean subdiaphragmatic to mean cervical endoneurial area is 0.20 in humans and 0.42 in pigs, and the ratio of mean nerve diameters is 0.87 and 0.75.
outcomes.quote: The ratios of the mean endoneurial area of the subdiaphragmatic VN to the cervical VN were 0.20, 0.42, and 0.32 for human, pig, and rat, respectively ... where the ratios of the mean diameter of the subdiaphragmatic VN to the cervical VN were 0.87, 0.75, and 0.68 for human, pig, and rat, respectively.
outcomes.notes: Endoneurial area ratios 0.198 (human) and 0.421 (pig), nerve diameter ratios 0.873 and 0.746, all within 10%.
outcomes.where: SPARC Portal, Pelot et al. (2020a) for human and (2020f) for pig MT; identifiers not in the text read

outcomes.statement: Nerve and fascicle diameters are more consistent across samples in pigs (and rats) than in humans.
outcomes.quote: Qualitatively, the nerve and fascicle diameters were more consistent across samples for the pig nerves than for the humans nerves ( Figure 6 )
outcomes.notes: Coefficient of variation of nerve diameter human 0.239, pig 0.089, rat 0.097 cervically and 0.189, 0.099, 0.110 subdiaphragmatically; of per-sample mean fascicle diameter 0.314, 0.077, 0.098 and 0.662, 0.141, 0.109. Human exceeds pig and rat on both measures at both levels (reading a), and pig under reading (b) (fascicle range CV 0.500 against 0.166, 0.853 against 0.192).
deviations: The coefficient of variation is the claims file's reading of the paper's qualitative comparison.

outcomes.statement: Human cervical fascicle numbers and endoneurial areas match prior reports while the nerve areas and diameters are generally smaller; human subdiaphragmatic sizes match prior reports; pig fascicle numbers match literature, with slightly smaller mean diameters.
outcomes.quote: The numbers of fascicles and endoneurial cross-sectional areas of the human cervical VNs were comparable to previous reports, but the nerve cross-sectional areas and effective diameters were generally smaller, albeit with overlapping ranges.
outcomes.notes: Literature values from Supplement 4 (Data_Sheet_2.xlsx), whose summaries of this paper's data equal the values measured here. 8 of the claim's 10 parts hold. Human cervical fascicles 6.67 +/- 4.5 contain all seven published means (5.0 to 9.14); human cervical nerve area 3.05 mm2 and diameter 1.92 mm are below every published mean (3.20 to 8.45 mm2, 2.02 to 3.28 mm) and below 3.0 mm; the human anterior subdiaphragmatic area and diameter contain the anterior published means; pig fascicles contain the published 46 and 43; pig diameters 2.20 and 1.64 mm are below the published 2.93 and 2.09 mm. Two parts fail; the human cervical endoneurial area 0.922 +/- 0.337 mm2 does not contain Seki et al.'s 1.32 and 1.84 mm2 (it contains Verlinden et al.'s 0.75 and 1.09), and the human cervical nerve area range (0.83 to 5.09 mm2) does not reach Verlinden et al.'s right-side spread (6.0 to 10.9 mm2). Against left-side rows only (this paper's samples are left cervical), 5 of the 6 human cervical parts hold; the ranges overlap and the endoneurial area still fails on Seki et al.'s left 1.32 mm2, so the outcome is the same. Fewer subdiaphragmatic fascicles than the posterior study (4.89 against 16) holds but is in the Results, not the claim's statement, and is not counted.
deviations: Supplement 4 was not under paper/; it is read from Europe PMC's supplementary files of the version of record (PMC7672126) and checked by SHA-256.
Each published mean is judged against this paper's mean +/- SD, the claims file's reading of Figure 7; the overlap of ranges uses the published spreads where Supplement 4 gives one.

Every published row is used, left and right, as the Results say the comparison includes "data published for both left/right and anterior/posterior VNs" and Figure 7 plots them; left-side rows only are a variant.
outcomes.where: SPARC Portal, Pelot et al. (2020a, 2020f); literature values in Supplement 4 (not in the text read)

outcomes.statement: Rat cervical nerve diameters and areas agree with published data, while the rat subdiaphragmatic nerves are slightly larger than prior data.
outcomes.quote: The nerve diameters and cross-sectional areas of the rat cervical VNs compared well to published data, while our rat subdiaphragmatic nerves were slightly larger than prior data
outcomes.notes: Rat subdiaphragmatic nerves are larger than every published value (diameter 0.135 mm against 0.086 to 0.109 mm, area 0.0145 against 0.0058 to 0.0093 mm2, Prechtl and Powley 1985). The cervical part fails the claims file's rule with every published row; one of four published diameter means (0.281 mm, Licursi de Alcantara et al., left) and one of four area means (0.0620 mm2, the same study) lie within the rat mean +/- SD (0.258 +/- 0.025 mm, 0.0526 +/- 0.0102 mm2); the others are 0.226, 0.284 and 0.299 mm. The rows 0.2843 mm and 0.0400 mm2 have no side or n in Supplement 4; their notes say they are Fazan and Lachat's right-side means converted between area and diameter ('Calculated mean(d_nerve) from mean(A_nerve)'). Without them the cervical part still fails. Against left-side rows only (Licursi de Alcantara et al.) it holds, and the claim would be reproduced; the readings give different outcomes, and the main one uses every row. Three of four published means lie within the range of the nine samples.
deviations: Literature values from Supplement 4, read from Europe PMC (PMC7672126).
The judgement rules are the claims file's reading of Figure 7.

Every published row is used, left and right, as the Results say the comparison includes "data published for both left/right and anterior/posterior VNs" and Figure 7 plots both sides; left-side rows only, under which the claim is reproduced, and the rows without Supplement 4's converted values are variants. The outcome rests on this choice.

outcomes.statement: For a given fascicle diameter, human fascicles have the thickest perineurium and rat fascicles the thinnest.
outcomes.quote: For a given fascicle diameter, the human samples had the thickest perineurium while the rat samples had the thinnest perineurium.
outcomes.notes: Over the diameters common to the three species (32.0 to 284.1 um) the human fit lies above the pig fit (by at least 7.43 um) and the pig above the rat (by at least 2.47 um); at 250 um 19.76, 9.81 and 4.60 um. Measured thicknesses of 200 to 300 um fascicles have medians 19.64 (human), 9.93 (pig) and 4.54 um (rat).
deviations: Pig IF thicknesses from SPARC:89's PigIFMorphology.mat, not recomputed from its traces.

outcomes.statement: The ratio of perineurium thickness to fascicle diameter decreases as fascicle diameter increases, particularly in humans and pigs.
outcomes.quote: The ratio of perineurium thickness to fascicle diameter decreased with increased fascicle diameter, particularly for the human and pig samples ( Figure 9B ).
outcomes.notes: The fitted ratio decreases over each species' range (human 1.58 to 0.047, pig 0.265 to 0.037, rat 0.056 to 0.018); Spearman correlation of the ratio with diameter human -0.919, pig -0.601, rat -0.779.

outcomes.statement: The fit of perineurium thickness against fascicle diameter for 73 human non-peanut fascicles has R2 = 0.75.
outcomes.quote: We fit the data from 73 human fascicles (excluding fascicles with more than one inner perineurium trace for a given outer perineurium trace, i.e., peanut fascicles) as ... with d fasc in microns, yielding R 2 = 0.75.
outcomes.notes: 73 human non-peanut fascicles; thickness = 0.03702 d + 10.505 um, R2 = 0.749. Through zero R2 = 0.168, quadratic 0.787.
deviations: The fit form is the paper's code's: DataPlotting_v4.m fits fittype('poly1') to the rat and human data (the human block is commented out but the same).
outcomes.where: SPARC Portal, Pelot et al. (2020a); identifier not in the text read

outcomes.statement: The fit of perineurium thickness against fascicle diameter for 284 pig non-peanut fascicles (IF) has R2 = 0.30.
outcomes.quote: We fit the data from 284 pig non-peanut fascicles as ... with d fasc in microns, yielding R 2 = 0.30.
outcomes.notes: 284 pig non-peanut IF fascicles; thickness = 0.02547 d + 3.440 um, R2 = 0.298, the value SPARC:89's PigIFMorphology.mat stores for its own fit (0.2984, 282 residual degrees of freedom).
deviations: Diameters and thicknesses from PigIFMorphology.mat, not recomputed from the IF traces (the IF folders have no ScaleLength file; SegmentationAnalysis_v2.m sets 500 um).
outcomes.where: SPARC Portal, Pelot et al. (2020b); identifier not in the text read

outcomes.statement: The fit of perineurium thickness against fascicle diameter for 22 rat fascicles has R2 = 0.77.
outcomes.quote: We fit the data from 22 rat fascicles as ... with d fasc in microns, yielding R 2 = 0.77.
outcomes.notes: All 22 rat fascicles with a thickness (reading a), fitted as the paper's code does (DataPlotting_v4.m, fittype('poly1') on both levels pooled), give thickness = 0.01292 d + 1.367 um with R2 = 0.765. With the 18 largest fascicles R2 = 0.664; through zero 0.510; quadratic 0.767.
deviations: The fascicle set and fit form, open in the claims file, are taken from DataPlotting_v4.m ('Fit rat perineurium data'), which is in the dataset.

outcomes.statement: In the human and pig vagus nerves, larger fascicles have thicker perineurium.
outcomes.quote: our data also showed thicker perineurium for larger fascicles, as well as thicker perineurium as a proportion of fascicle diameter for smaller fascicles.
outcomes.notes: Fitted slopes positive, human 0.0370 (95% CI 0.0320 to 0.0421) and pig 0.0255 (0.0209 to 0.0300); Spearman correlations 0.918 and 0.545. Rats too (0.0129, rho 0.864).
outcomes.where: SPARC Portal, Pelot et al. (2020a) for human and (2020b) for pig IF; identifiers not in the text read

outcomes.statement: The relationship between perineurium thickness and fascicle diameter does not differ between cervical and subdiaphragmatic nerves in any of the three species.
outcomes.quote: The data did not suggest a difference in the relationship between perineurium thickness and fascicle diameter for cervical versus subdiaphragmatic nerves for any of the three species.
outcomes.notes: Reading (a) the 95% bounds of the level-wise fits do not overlap for the human slope (0.0318 [0.0248, 0.0388] cervical against 0.0558 [0.0494, 0.0622] subdiaphragmatic) nor for the pig intercept (5.26 [4.14, 6.39] against 3.16 [2.67, 3.65] um); both rat coefficients overlap. Reading (b) agrees, human p = 2.4e-07, pig p = 3.1e-09, rat p = 0.87. The rat part, testable on the dataset alone, holds.
deviations: The paper names no test for 'did not suggest a difference'; the tests are the claims file's.

outcomes.statement: Refitting all 777 fascicles of Sunderland and Bradley (1952) gives a zero-intercept slope of 2.75% of fascicle diameter for perineurium thickness, with R2 = 0.51.
outcomes.source: Results, paragraphs 13 and 14 (Eq. 4); Discussion, paragraph 7; Figure 9C and 9D
outcomes.quote: We re-analyzed the original ( Sunderland and Bradley, 1952 ) data, including all 777 fascicles ... and identified the slope of the best-fit line with zero intercept as 2.75% ( R 2 = 0.51)
outcomes.notes: The 777 fascicles of files/code/Sunderland1984.mat in SPARC:65 give a zero-intercept slope of 2.750% with R2 = 0.510 (about the mean, as MATLAB's fit computes it); the uncentred R2 is 0.853.
deviations: The Sunderland and Bradley (1952) table is taken from the paper's own transcription in SPARC:65's code folder, not from the 1952 paper.
outcomes.where: Sunderland and Bradley (1952), the published human somatic nerve fascicle measurements; no archive identifier

outcomes.statement: Rat perineurium thickness is close to the published 3% of fascicle diameter, slightly thicker for smaller fascicles and thinner for larger ones.
outcomes.quote: While we found that the rat perineurium thickness was similar to this published relationship, albeit slightly thicker for smaller fascicle diameters and thinner for larger fascicle diameters
outcomes.notes: Against the 3% line the rat fit over the line runs from 1.856 at 32.0 um to 0.591 at 284.1 um, within a factor of two, above the line for small fascicles and below for large ones (crossing at 80.1 um). Against 2.75% the ratio reaches 2.024 at the smallest diameter, just outside; the claim holds under the 3% reading.
deviations: 'Similar' as within a factor of two is the claims file's reading.

outcomes.statement: Human and pig vagal perineurium is substantially thicker than the 3% of fascicle diameter found for human somatic nerves, especially for smaller fascicles.
outcomes.quote: the human and pig perineurium was substantially thicker, especially for smaller fascicles ( Figure 9B )
outcomes.notes: Median ratio of thickness to diameter 0.0948 (human) and 0.0527 (pig), above 0.03; median excess below the species' median diameter 0.1061 and 0.0329, above it 0.0379 and 0.0160. Rats are below the line (0.0214).
deviations: The measure is the claims file's reading of Figure 9B.
outcomes.where: SPARC Portal, Pelot et al. (2020a) for human and (2020b) for pig IF; identifiers not in the text read

outcomes.statement: Pig fascicle diameters from anti-fibronectin IF (14 to 303 um, mean 123, median 123, interquartile range 91 to 155 um) are consistent with those from MT (5 to 399 um, mean 135, median 130, interquartile range 96 to 168 um).
outcomes.quote: Note that the fascicle diameters for the pig anti-fibronectin IF ( Figures 9A,B ; 14 to 303 μm, mean = 123 μm, median = 123 μm, interquartile range = 91 to 155 μm) are consistent with the MT data ( Figure 6 ; 5 to 399 μm, mean = 135 μm, median = 130 μm, interquartile range = 96 to 168 μm).
outcomes.notes: IF non-peanut (284) 14.4 to 302.8 um, mean 123.3, median 123.1, interquartile range 88.1 to 152.5; MT (766) 23.7 to 399.1 um, mean 134.6, median 129.5, interquartile range 95.7 to 167.7. All within the criterion, which tests that each range lies within the reported one widened by 10% of each bound. Read bound by bound, the MT minimum fails, 23.7 um against the paper's 5 um; SPARC:64's output file has no fascicle below 23.7 um (the five smallest are 23.7 to 31.2 um), so the 5 um fascicle is not in the deposited data.
deviations: Interquartile range by linear interpolation (numpy default), a standard choice; MATLAB's prctile method gives 88.0 to 152.6 and 95.6 to 167.7.
outcomes.where: SPARC Portal, Pelot et al. (2020b) for pig IF and (2020f) for pig MT; identifiers not in the text read

outcomes.statement: Human IHC micrographs have 60 cervical inner perineurium traces (27 bundles in 10 peanut fascicles) and 44 subdiaphragmatic (4 in 2); pig IF micrographs have 210 cervical (57 in 25) and 179 subdiaphragmatic (48 in 19).
outcomes.quote: For the human anti-claudin-1 IHC micrographs, the cervical level had 60 fascicles total (inner perineurium traces) of which 27 were intrafascicular bundles in 10 peanut fascicles; the subdiaphragmatic level had 44 fascicles total (inner perineurium traces) of which 4 were intrafascicular bundles in 2 peanut fascicles.
outcomes.notes: Human traces (SPARC:65) give 60 cervical inner traces with 27 bundles in 10 peanut fascicles and 44 subdiaphragmatic with 4 in 2, as the legend says. Pig IF traces (SPARC:89), counted as its SegmentationAnalysis_v2.m counts them (hole boundaries included), give 210 cervical with 57 bundles in 24 peanut fascicles, where the legend says 25, and 179 subdiaphragmatic with 48 in 19. 11 of 12 counts match. Per sample the cervical peanut fascicles are 4, 8, 6 and 6 by both counting rules, so the 25th is not found in any sample; the code's own count (Nouterperi_peanut_values) is not saved in PigIFMorphology.mat. Counting objects only, the subdiaphragmatic pig traces give 178 (one inner mask has a hole). Non-peanut sums 73 and 284, the fits' counts.
deviations: The pig counts follow SPARC:89's code, which counts hole boundaries of the masks as traces.
outcomes.where: SPARC Portal, Pelot et al. (2020a) for human and (2020b) for pig IF; identifiers not in the text read

outcomes.statement: The morphology metrics show no trend with age in any species.
outcomes.quote: Our morphology metrics did not show trends with age for any species ( Supplement 6 )
outcomes.notes: Of 26 per-species, per-level correlations with age, three have Pearson p < 0.05 (reading a), all in pigs; cervical endoneurium proportion r = -0.72 (p = 0.029), subdiaphragmatic nerve diameter r = 0.75 (p = 0.019), subdiaphragmatic mean fascicle diameter r = 0.69 (p = 0.039). Spearman (reading b) finds one, human subdiaphragmatic mean fascicle diameter (rho = -0.69, p = 0.041). 1.3 would be expected by chance; the tests are uncorrected, as the criterion names them, and the pig ages take four values (10.5 to 15 weeks). With a Holm correction no test is below 0.05 (smallest corrected p 0.499 over the 26 tests, 0.154 within species), which would make the claim reproduced. The rat part shows no trend. Whether the criterion should correct for the number of tests is asked of a reader (questions/pelot-2020.yaml).
deviations: Supplement 6 (Europe PMC supplementary PDF, printed in the notebook) is one figure, 'Nerve morphology metrics versus age', with no test, so the paper's judgement is visual; the tests are the claims file's.
Human ages '90+ years' entered as 99, as DataExtraction_v3.m does.

outcomes.statement: The rat cervical carotid sheath holds up to six fascicles, of which the largest, taken as the vagus, was segmented.
outcomes.quote: The rat cervical VN was identified as monofascicular in prior studies ( Fazan and Lachat, 1997 ; Licursi de Alcântara et al., 2008 ), but we observed up to six fascicles within the carotid sheath ( Supplementary Figure 16 ).
outcomes.notes: The data are there in part. The derivative folder holds the nine cervical micrographs (JPEG 2000, files/derivative/sub-*/sam-*/*MT20x.jp2), which the notebook shows at 1/8 resolution with the traced vagus drawn over them; every trace lies within its image, and the legend of Supplementary Figure 16 says the micrographs also show other nerves of the carotid sheath. But each cervical PeriMask, and each Neurolucida file (MergeMask.xml), holds only the vagus, and the paper does not say how the other bundles were identified or counted. Counting them here would be the attempt's own visual judgement, not a measurement from the data, so the claim is not tested. A segmentation or labels of the other bundles would make it testable. The criterion's two conditions ("Testable only if the dataset holds the cervical micrographs", "Not testable when only the vagus is traced") disagree for this dataset; this is asked of a reader in questions/pelot-2020.yaml.

findings.statement: files/derivative/RatVNMorphology_OutputMetrics.mat, described in the derivative manifest as the rat morphology output metrics, is an older output (written 2020-03-03) that holds 54 samples of all three species (human C, pig P and rat R). Its rat values are not those of the primary traces or of the paper; cervical nerve diameters are up to 8.5 um larger (R22-3, 245.2 against 236.7 um) and the multifascicular samples use the connective tissue boundary. The code folder's file of the same name (2020-09-05) matches the traces and the paper.

The code folder's RatVNMorphology_OutputMetrics.mat keeps only 7 of the 22 rat perineurium thicknesses (thkperi_um is overwritten per sex and level category in DataPlotting_v4.m), so the thicknesses behind the rat perineurium fit are recoverable only by re-measuring the traces.
The readme gives the rats' ages as 65 to 268 days; subjects.xlsx and the paper give 75 to 268 days.

samples.xlsx describes the subdiaphragmatic samples as 'subdiaphragmatic vagus nerve' without saying they are the anterior trunk, which only the readme and the code's file names give. R17-1 has a NerveMask although it is monofascicular, and nothing says whether it is meant to be used.

verifications.reviewed: Round 1. The first executed notebook with the conclusion cells and the summary removed, the helper module and the claims file, with the paper under paper/. The verifier browsed SPARC:60 version 5 on Pennsieve for the blocked claim and tested bwboundaries, polyarea, fit_poly1, reml_unbounded and tukey on synthetic inputs. Its report gave its own outcome for each of the 35 claims; all agree with the record as it then stood.

verifications.reviewed: Round 2. The full executed notebook of the round-1 revision, with its conclusions and summary, the helper module, the claims file and the attempt record, with the paper under paper/. The verifier agreed with 34 of the 35 outcomes and with fascicles-larger-cervical only with qualification. It also found the Summary's sentence on C54-3 ("the published code would measure the image frame (3.57 mm) in place of the nerve (1.62 mm)") unsupported, as 3.57 appears in no output and cell 12 shows the code's own output file has 1615 um for C54-3; the Summary now says the mask is inverted and that its complement gives the code folder's 1615 um. Every other Result sentence, the rest of the Summary, the README and the record's notes it found to agree with the printed outputs, and the round-1 reasons to be stated accurately.

verifications.reviewed: Round 3. The proposed change of outcome on fascicles-larger-cervical, the one claim with a proposal, and the analysis behind it in the full executed notebook of the round-2 revision (cells 18, 38, 53, 54, 56, 59 and 62), with the claims file and the attempt record. Nothing else was reviewed.

paper_notes.statement: The Methods use 'only the largest fascicle in each rat sample' for all statistics, but DataPlotting_v4.m takes the first inner perineurium trace in its order as the rat fascicle diameter (it sorts only the outer diameters). In R22-1 that trace is 39.35 um against a largest fascicle of 105.76 um, and in R23-1 142.15 against 147.47 um. The paper's rat subdiaphragmatic fascicle diameter, 0.121 +/- 0.032 mm, and its fascicle diameter F values (8.989, 51.88, 5.273, reproduced here with the code's values) rest on these values; with the largest fascicles they are 0.129 +/- 0.014 mm and F = 9.59, 46.5 and 4.93.

The Discussion's rat ratios of subdiaphragmatic to cervical means (endoneurial area 0.32, nerve diameter 0.68) are reproduced only with all segmented fascicles and the connective tissue boundary of the multifascicular samples (0.317 and 0.678), while the Methods say all rat statistics use the largest fascicle; with it the ratios are 0.270 and 0.525, and the Results' own means give 0.52.

Question for the authors. Which JMP settings were used for the mixed models? Unbounded variance components (the nerve diameter subject variance estimate is negative, -0.052) with Kenward-Roger tests computed on the observed REML information give the paper's F and p for all nine effects reported (nerve diameter 577.0, 11.01, 2.4455 against 577.1, 11.01, 2.445); with the variance bounded at zero the nerve diameter interaction becomes significant (p = 0.024). Is that what JMP did, and how was the pig cervical against subdiaphragmatic Tukey p of 0.0009 obtained? Under the same test it is 0.055 (3.74 degrees of freedom), and it would need about 25 degrees of freedom to be 0.0009.

Question for the authors. What test supports 'the data did not suggest a difference in the relationship between perineurium thickness and fascicle diameter for cervical versus subdiaphragmatic nerves'? Fitting each level separately, the 95% bounds of the human slope (0.032 against 0.056) and of the pig intercept (5.3 against 3.2 um) do not overlap, and an F test of level terms gives p < 1e-6 for both; only the rat fits agree.

Question for the authors. What test is behind 'our morphology metrics did not show trends with age' ? Supplement 6 shows the metrics against age without a test. Uncorrected Pearson correlations per species and level find 3 of 26 with p < 0.05, all in pigs, whose ages take four values.

entries.name: pelot-2020
entries.title: Vagus nerve morphology of human, pig and rat (Pelot et al. 2020)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Pelot, Goldhagen, Cariello, Musselman, Clissold, Ezzell and Grill (2020) on SPARC dataset 60, version 5, which holds the segmented traces of nine left cervical and nine anterior subdiaphragmatic rat vagus nerve samples and the paper's MATLAB code. The rat nerve and fascicle diameters, fascicle counts, tissue proportions and perineurium fit are measured from the traces with the paper's method. The comparisons with human and pig use the paper's sister datasets, SPARC 65 (human traces), 64 (pig Masson's trichrome) and 89 (pig anti-fibronectin), for the mixed model ANOVAs, Tukey tests and perineurium fits, and Supplement 4 of the paper for the literature comparisons.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Pelot et al. (2020) from SPARC dataset 60 and its sister datasets
